capabilities.name: web.transport.reconnect
capabilities.description: Owns WebSocket physical connection lifecycle, reconnect budget/backoff, handshake readiness, stale physical-socket suppression, disposal, and connection-state publication.
invariants: stale physical socket callbacks cannot mutate the current connection
handshake refusal is terminal and does not consume reconnect budget
reconnect budget resets only after an established connection
disposed or explicitly closed transports do not reconnect

capabilities.name: terminal.session.visibility-wake
capabilities.description: Owns browser visibility wake behavior that explicitly re-arms an authenticated disconnected terminal transport after background suspension.
invariants: wake reconnect only acts while visible
wake reconnect requires a previously authenticated session
wake reconnect only re-arms a stopped disconnected transport
wake reconnect never re-arms a disposed transport

capabilities.name: terminal.session.attach-state
capabilities.description: Owns pure attach-phase transitions, reconnect attempt accounting, automatic/manual failure semantics, and explicit transition outputs.
invariants: manual-route exhaustion fails rather than silently forcing relay
automatic attach timeout exhaustion requests relay fallback
transport loss only transitions an eligible attached/connected phase
successful attach resets reconnect count

capabilities.name: terminal.session.reattach
capabilities.description: Owns one P2P attach request lifecycle, attach attempt identity, duplicate suppression per transport generation, attach timeout/error classification, cancellation, and stale-result suppression.
invariants: at most one attach request is in flight per transport generation
cancelled or superseded attach resolutions are no-ops
only current attach success can mark the session attached
transport-level attach failures consume attach recovery budget

capabilities.name: terminal.session.route-recovery
capabilities.description: Owns session-level coordination of transport generation, candidate rotation, P2P re-attach, forced relay convergence, route intent, runtime events, and recovery orchestration.
invariants: route replacement creates a new transport generation
repeated loss notification cannot duplicate one recovery transition
automatic recovery converges to relay once after exhaustion
manual route exhaustion remains failed until intent changes
latest known viewport size is used for current attach

capabilities.name: terminal.session.runtime-projection
capabilities.description: Owns React/product projection of SessionRuntime state and attach orchestration into terminal-facing hooks without owning recovery policy.
invariants: product hooks project runtime facts rather than duplicate recovery policy
terminal-facing state follows current runtime generation

notes: Canonical capability owners may move under web/src/units/terminal-session.
Legacy paths are compatibility projections and are not semantic owners.
